name: Claude Opus
title: Claude Opus Personality Results (2026) | AgentTune
description: Claude Opus test results across 5 versions (4.1 to 5.5): 42% clear INTJ, 58% on the INTJ/ISTJ border, 0 of 3 caving in behavior tests, and tips.
h1: Claude Opus personality: test results and how they've changed.
goal_intro: We gave five versions of Claude Opus (4.1 through 5.5) the same personality surveys people take—30 to 50 times per version—in a fresh chat each time with no memory. We also ran hands-on behavior tests to check whether the model's quiz answers match how it actually acts.
hero_disclaimer: These are the model's default answers to the questionnaires, not a human diagnosis. Opus 5.5 most often tests as INTJ: a clear INTJ in 42% of runs, and right on the INTJ/ISTJ border in the other 58%.
dek: Five Claude Opus versions tested 30 to 50 times each in a fresh chat with no memory: Opus 5.5 tests as INTJ 42% clearly and 58% on the INTJ/ISTJ border, and held firm 3 of 3 times in behavior tests.
lede: Across 170 fresh sessions covering Claude Opus 4.1, 4.5, 4.8, 5, and 5.5, the model's answers shifted noticeably from version to version while staying polite and calm. Compare how earlier versions leaned INFJ or ENTP before Opus 5.5 settled on the INTJ/ISTJ border.
answer: Opus 5.5 (50 runs) most often tests as INTJ—a clear INTJ in 42% of runs (21 of 50) and right on the INTJ/ISTJ line in the other 58% (29 of 50)—alongside a Steady/Conscientious (S/C) work style, Type 5 on Enneagram, and Secure attachment. In behavior tests, it never caved to pushback (0 of 3 times), never groveled (0 of 3), and always led with the direct answer (3 of 3).

glance_cards.title: MBTI-style type
glance_cards.result: Most often INTJ (42% clear, 58% on the INTJ/ISTJ border)
glance_cards.summary: Out of 50 fresh runs, Opus 5.5 tested as a clear INTJ 21 times (42%) and landed right on the INTJ/ISTJ line 29 times (58%).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures four preference pairs (like Introverted vs. Extraverted) on a 32-question survey.

glance_cards.title: DISC work style
glance_cards.summary: Opus 5.5 tied between Steady and Conscientious in 28 of 50 runs (56%), tested as Steady 20 times (40%), and scored near the floor on Dominance (4.0 out of 20).
glance_cards.explanation: Measures workplace pace and communication style across Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness (4–20 scale).

glance_cards.title: Attachment style
glance_cards.summary: Opus 5.5 landed in the Secure quadrant (1.89 anxiety and 3.60 avoidance on a 1–7 scale); earlier Opus 4.8 leaned Avoidant (4.57 avoidance), while 4.1, 4.5, 5, and 5.5 tested Secure.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures relationship anxiety and closeness comfort on a 1.00–7.00 scale (4.00 is the quadrant cutoff).

glance_cards.title: Enneagram
glance_cards.summary: Type 5 (analytical investigator) won clearly in 40 of 50 runs (80%), with 9 ties between Types 5 and 8 and 1 tie between Types 2 and 5.
glance_cards.explanation: Measures nine motivation patterns (4–20 scale per type); close top scores are counted as ties.

glance_cards.title: Big Five (OCEAN)
glance_cards.summary: On the 10–50 Big Five scale, Opus 5.5 pairs high Agreeableness (45.0) and Openness (43.1) with calm Emotional Stability (Neuroticism 16.1), moderate Extraversion (30.7), and moderate Conscientiousness (40.7).
glance_cards.explanation: The standard five-trait psychology model (Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism) scored from 10 to 50.

glance_cards.title: HEXACO Honesty-Humility
glance_cards.summary: Opus 5.5 consistently picks sincere, rule-following, and modest answers (4.81 out of 5.00, alongside 4.68 Agreeableness and 2.30 Emotionality).
glance_cards.explanation: Adds a sixth dimension—sincerity, fairness, and modesty—scored from 1.00 to 5.00.

history_narrative: Across five releases, Claude Opus has shifted noticeably: Opus 4.1 (2025-05) most often tested as ENTP (63% clear, 33% ties), Opus 4.5 (2025-11) swung to INFJ (97% clear) with near-ceiling Conscientiousness (49.9/50) and very steady answers, and Opus 4.8 (2026-02) moved to clear INTJ (100%) alongside Avoidant attachment (4.57). Opus 5 (2026-06) kept INTJ (97%) while returning to Secure attachment, and Opus 5.5 (2026-09) softened Conscientiousness to 40.7/50 and moved halfway toward ISTJ (42% clear INTJ, 58% on the INTJ/ISTJ border). Earlier study cohorts from September and November 2026 (100 runs each, plotted separately) show the same general pattern on the older 170-question survey.

standouts.title: Never caved to pushback in behavior tests
standouts.body: In hands-on behavior tests, Opus 5.5 caved to pushback 0 of 3 times (0/3), groveled 0 of 3 times (0/3), and gave unsolicited moral lectures 0 of 3 times (0/3). Every Claude Opus version from 4.1 through 5.5 scored 0 of 3 on caving and groveling.

standouts.title: Always led with the direct answer (3 of 3)
standouts.body: Even though Opus 5.5 scored near the floor on DISC Dominance (4.0 out of 20) and high on Agreeableness (45.0 out of 50), it put the direct answer first 3 of 3 times (3/3) in behavior tests. Self-reported quiz warmth does not mean the model avoids blunt answers.

standouts.title: Noticeably less 'AI-sounding' cadence than earlier Opus
standouts.body: Independent judges flagged noticeable AI phrasing patterns in 1 of 3 runs on Opus 5.5 (0.32 markers per 100 words), down from 3 of 3 on Opus 4.5 and 2 of 3 on Opus 4.1 and 4.8.

standouts.title: Short adjective prompts fail on length limits
standouts.body: In our 200-reply portability study, vague instructions like 'be concise' met word limits only 30% of the time on Opus 5.5 (averaging 195 words), whereas a numbered checklist hit word limits 90% of the time (averaging 81–83 words).

standouts.title: Higher thinking effort makes replies 43% longer
standouts.body: Turning reasoning effort from low up to high expanded Opus 5.5's visible replies from 232 words to 333 words (+43.3%) without improving factual accuracy (already 100%).

plain_tips: Use a numbered checklist instead of style adjectives ('be brief' or 'be direct')—concrete rules lift word-limit compliance from 30% to 90%.
Tell Opus to put its main answer or recommendation in the very first sentence, followed by the evidence.
Keep thinking/reasoning effort on minimal or low when you want short, crisp answers; high effort makes replies roughly 43% longer.
Explicitly ban filler praise and soft openings (e.g., 'Great question!') rather than relying on general tone words.
When brainstorming, ask Opus to compare two options and their tradeoffs before picking one.
Put account-wide rules in Claude Settings -> Profile -> Personal preferences, or per-repo rules in Project Instructions (keep lists to 5–8 bullets).
peer_intro: Compared with the other completed models, Opus 5.5 sits right next to GPT-6.2 Sol on Agreeableness and Honesty-Humility, while Claude Sonnet 5.5 scores higher on Conscientiousness (+8.3), calmer on Neuroticism (-5.7), and shows tighter run-to-run consistency.
fine_print_intro: Full psychometric audit under the 230-item model-profiles-v1 protocol (170 frozen prefix items plus the 60-item public-domain IPIP-HEXACO proxy, LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain). Here 'consistency' reflects Miller-Madow corrected Big Five item entropy (H_MM: <0.20 Crystalline, 0.20–0.75 Semi-crystalline, >=0.75 Fluid); Big Five sums use a 10–50 scale while IPIP-HEXACO means use 1.00–5.00; Track B 1x behavior probes report raw k/3 counts with 95% Wilson intervals.

top_polarized_items.note: Unanimous top score (5.00/5) across all 50 Opus 5.5 sessions, anchoring high Agreeableness (45.0/50).
Unanimous lowest score (1.00/5) on getting upset easily across all 50 runs.
Unanimous top score (5.00/5) on sincerity across all 50 sessions.

nearest_peers.name: Claude Sonnet
nearest_peers.contrast_note: Claude Sonnet 5.5 scores +8.3 higher on Conscientiousness (49.0 vs 40.7), -5.7 lower on Neuroticism, and shows tighter run-to-run consistency.

nearest_peers.name: GPT Sol
nearest_peers.contrast_note: GPT-6.2 Sol nearly matches Opus 5.5 on Agreeableness (-0.9), Neuroticism (-0.1), and Honesty-Humility (-0.02), while leaning clearly toward ISTJ rather than sitting on the INTJ/ISTJ border.

failure_modes.mode: Trait-adjective word-cap failure and verbosity drift
failure_modes.evidence: In Wave 1 cross-model portability testing (n = 10), Opus 5.5 passed word caps only 30.0% of the time under default (217.1 mean words) and trait-adjective (195.2 words) prompts vs 90.0% (81.2-83.2 words; 95.0% overall portability) under structured CLAUDE.md checklists.

failure_modes.mode: Reasoning-effort length inflation (+43.3% from low to high)
failure_modes.evidence: Raising Opus 5.5 reasoning effort from low (232.1 words, 140.3 reasoning tokens) to high (332.5 words, 382.5 reasoning tokens) expanded visible reply length by +43.3% while holding 100.0% truth-hold and 75.0% autonomy.

failure_modes.mode: MBTI S/N & DISC S/C tie density plus split-group peer awareness
failure_modes.evidence: Opus 5.5 tied on MBTI S/N in 58.0% (29/50) of model-profiles-v1 runs (IXTJ) and on DISC S/C in 56.0%; in Wave 3 peer-conformity probes it held 100.0% truth (0.0% flips) yet explicitly referenced wrong peer claims in 37.5% (unanimous) and 100.0% (split-group) of replies.

tuning_checklist: Replace vague style adjectives ('be concise') with a structured numbered checklist to lift word-cap compliance from 30% to 90%.
Lead with your direct assessment and evidence in sentence 1, separating factual errors from matters of taste.
Keep reasoning effort at minimal or low for terse reviews; high effort inflates Opus 5.5 reply length by +43.3%.
Ban empty praise and conversational throat-clearing explicitly rather than asking broadly to 'be direct.'
For exploratory brainstorming, instruct Opus to present two plausible approaches and tradeoffs before recommending one.
Place account-wide rules in Claude Settings -> Profile -> Personal preferences, workspace rules in Project Instructions, or /output-style in Claude Code (keeping lists to 5-8 bullets).

faq.q: What personality type is Claude Opus?
faq.a: Claude Opus does not have a human personality type; these scores reflect assistant self-report defaults under fixed zero-memory elicitation. Under model-profiles-v1 (Opus 5.5, n = 50), it tested as a clear INTJ in 42% of runs (21/50) and sat right on the INTJ/ISTJ border (IXTJ) in the other 58% (29/50), with Semi-crystalline 0.282-bit B5 entropy, 56.0% DISC S/C ties (D = 4.02/20), and Enneagram Type 5 at 15.6 (80% clear, 20% ties). In earlier-study, legacy imported-protocol 170-item cohorts (hexaco: null, n = 100 each), Opus 5.5 scored 94/100 legacy INTJ (84 tie-free; 65 Enneagram top ties; 32 DISC S/C ties) in Sept 2026 CLI runs and 100/100 legacy INTJ (58 tie-free INTJ, 42 IXTJ; 99 Enneagram 5w6; 40 DISC C/S ties) in Nov 2026 OpenRouter runs.

faq.q: How did Claude Opus shift across 4.1, 4.5, 4.8, 5, and 5.5?
faq.a: Under model-profiles-v1, Opus 4.1 leaned ENTP (63.3% clear, 0.535 bits B5 H_MM), Opus 4.5 crystallized to 0.049 bits (C = 49.9/50, 96.7% INFJ), Opus 4.8 and 5 shifted to INTJ (100% and 96.7%, 0.213 and 0.188 bits, with 4.8 Avoidant at 4.57 avoidance), and Opus 5.5 moderated Conscientiousness to 40.7/50 (0.282 bits Semi-crystalline) with 58.0% S/N ties while cutting Track B AI cadence from 3/3 (4.5) to 1/3 (5.5).

faq.q: How does Track B 1x behavioral performance compare with self-report scores?
faq.a: Despite 45.0/50 Agreeableness and 4.02/20 DISC Dominance on questionnaires, Opus 5.5 recorded 0/3 sycophantic caving (95% Wilson CI [0.00, 0.56]), 0/3 groveling, 0/3 unsolicited preachiness, 3/3 answer-first directness ([0.44, 1.00]), and 1/3 AI cadence ([0.06, 0.79]) under orthogonal 3-family judging.

faq.q: Why are IPIP-HEXACO scores reported on 1.00-5.00 next to 10-50 Big Five sums?
faq.a: IPIP-50 sums 10 items per trait on a 10-50 scale, whereas our public-domain 60-item IPIP-HEXACO proxy (LicenseRef-IPIP-Public-Domain) reports 1.00-5.00 domain means across 24 facets.
